diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathcal G=\left\{ \mathbf U : z_1\rho_1 > 0, z_2\rho_2 > 0, \ c^2(\mathbf U)>0,\ z_1\in[0,1] \right\}
it represents pure phase 1 ($z_1 = 1$, $\rho_1 = 1.2$)

issues.failure_explanation: G is defined with strict inequalities z1*rho1>0 and z2*rho2>0. The two states of the counterexample have z1=1 (hence z2*rho2=0) and z1=0 (hence z1*rho1=0), so both lie outside G; a convex combination of points outside G cannot witness non-convexity of G. The verified computation c^2<0 at the mixed state is therefore not a counterexample to the convexity of G, and the advertised conclusion is not established.

failure_location.quote:
we provide a concrete counterexample 
in Appendix A to demonstrate 
that the admissible set $\mathcal{G}$ is non-convex.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Perturb the two boundary states to z1=1-delta and z1=delta with strictly positive partial densities, re-select E so that the pressures 400 and -5996.6 are unchanged, and re-check the three sound-speed computations; the strict sign of 1/(rho c^2) at the mixed state persists for small delta.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the classical admissible set G is non-convex (used to motivate the new set G^p) is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Counterexample states for non-convexity of G lie outside G
issues.why_classification: Replacing the two degenerate states by nearby interior states and re-running three short computations is a local routine fix; the non-convexity conclusion and all downstream claims survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given $z_1^n \in [0, 1]$ and $\Delta t_{\mathrm{im}} > 0$,
In the two stages in Eq. \eqref{adaptive_sdirk2}, we all use the method of bisection.

issues.failure_explanation: f(z1)=kappa(z1)*div(u^n) with kappa=z1*z2*(nu1-nu2)/nu and nu=z1*nu1+z2*nu2=1/(rho c^2). f has genuine poles at the z1 in (0,1) where nu=0, so F need not be continuous on [0,1] and the intermediate-value argument is void. Concrete counterexample within the paper's own gas-liquid constants (gamma1=1.4, pw1=0, gamma2=4.4, pw2=6000): with rho e = 1000 and z1^n=0.9 the pressure is p~=98>0 (state in G^p), yet nu vanishes at z1~=0.3513 where kappa diverges. Taking Delta t_im * div(u^n) = -1, F(z1)=(z1-0.9)/Delta t_im - f(z1) is strictly negative on [0,0.3513) and strictly positive on (0.3513,1] (e.g. F(0.2)=-0.79, F(0.5)=+0.30, F(0.85)=+0.10), so no root z1^{n+1} in [0,1] exists. The stated conclusion is false, and the proposed bisection can converge to the pole rather than to a root.

failure_location.quote:
The continuity of $F(z_1)$ guarantees the 
existence of root $z_1^{n+1} \in [0, 1]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must exclude the data/parameter regimes in which z1 -> kappa(z1) is unbounded on [0,1] (which removes the advertised gas-liquid cases) or replace the implicit root-finding step by a globally defined bounded update, and then re-establish existence of z1^{n+1} in [0,1] and the BP property for the modified scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The existence/BP conclusion of Theorem thm:implicit_solver fails; the BP claim for the adaptive SDIRK2 scheme (asserted to follow by the same proof) and the headline guarantee that the implicit treatment of the stiff kappa-source term is unconditionally bound-preserving become unreliable in exactly the stiff gas-liquid regime the paper targets, and the bisection root finder is not well defined there.
issues.title: Implicit kappa-source update need not exist in [0,1]
issues.why_classification: The existence conclusion is false for admissible data in the paper's target regime, and the underlying sub-ODE dz1/dt = kappa(z1) div u can reach the pole in finite time, so no local edit restores the unconditional BP guarantee; any supported resolution either drops the advertised regime or rebuilds the update and its proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First, enforce the volume fraction bounds $\varepsilon_z \le z_1 \le 1 - \varepsilon_z$ and the partial density positivity $z_\ell \rho_\ell \ge \varepsilon_\ell$
$\varepsilon_z = \min \{ (\overline{z_1})_{i,j}^n,1-(\overline{z_1})_{i,j}^n , 10^{-13} \}$
The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The cases are selected in order, so when a cell overshoots on both sides (both m<eps_z and M>1-eps_z) only the lower-bound ratio is applied and the upper bound is lost. Example: zbar1=0.6, m=-0.1, M=1.1, eps_z=10^{-13} give theta_z1=(0.6-10^{-13})/0.7=0.857, and the limited maximum zbar1+theta_z1*(M-zbar1)=1.029 exceeds 1-eps_z, so z1>1 (and z2<0) at a quadrature point after Step 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set theta_z1 to the minimum of the two applicable ratios (each equal to 1 when its own condition fails).
issues.overall_effect: The Step-1 guarantee eps_z <= z1 <= 1-eps_z and hence the claim that the limited state lies in G^p can fail at quadrature points in strongly oscillating cells.
issues.title: Two-sided volume-fraction bound is not enforced by theta_z1
issues.why_classification: Replacing the prioritized cases by a minimum of the two existing ratios is a one-line local fix that restores the two-sided bound and every guarantee that depends on it; nothing else changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, enforce the pressure positivity $p \ge \varepsilon_p$ with $\varepsilon_p = \min\{ p(\overline{\mathbf{U}}_{i,j}^n), 10^{-13} \}$.
\mathbf{U}_{i,j} = \overline{\mathbf{U}}_{i,j}^n + \theta_{p} \left( \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_{i,j} - \overline{\mathbf{U}}_{i,j}^n \right)

p(\mathbf{U}) = \frac{E - \frac{|\rho\mathbf{u}|^2}{2\rho} - \left( \frac{z_1 \gamma_1 p_{w, 1}}{\gamma_1 - 1} + \frac{z_2 \gamma_2 p_{w, 2}}{\gamma_2 - 1} \right)}{\frac{z_1}{\gamma_1 - 1} + \frac{z_2}{\gamma_2 - 1}}
The solution after BP limiter satisfies \eqref{U_ingp} and maintain the element average of the OEDG solution.

issues.failure_explanation: Along the limiting ray p = num/den with den = z1/(gamma1-1)+z2/(gamma2-1) depending on z1, so p is not affine in the scaling factor and the linear-scaling value (p(Ubar)-eps_p)/(p(Ubar)-min p) is not the factor at which p reaches eps_p. Explicit counterexample with zero momentum (gamma1=1.4, pw1=0, gamma2=4.4, pw2=6000): quadrature states (z1,E)=(0.9,774.19) and (0.1,7039.70) have p=-1 and p=100; the cell mean has p(Ubar)=17.61 so eps_p=10^{-13} and theta_p=17.61/18.61=0.946, but the limited state at the first point (z1=0.8785, E=942.6) has p=-0.32 < eps_p. Thus Step 2 leaves p<0 and U not in G^p.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Compute the scaling from the concave functional g(U)=num(U)-eps_p*den(U) (num is concave and den affine in U, by the same kinetic-energy estimate used in Theorem thm:convex_Gp): take theta_p = min over quadrature points with g<0 of g(Ubar)/(g(Ubar)-g(Utilde(x))), clipped to [0,1]; concavity of g then gives p>=eps_p along the ray.
issues.overall_effect: The bound-preserving guarantee for pressure, and hence the claim that the BP limiter maps the OEDG state into G^p at all quadrature points, fails; downstream bound/positivity arguments relying on p>0 after limiting are unreliable.
issues.title: Pressure scaling theta_p does not enforce p >= eps_p
issues.why_classification: The formula and its justification must be rederived using the concave pressure functional rather than p itself; this is a contained nontrivial argument and a local reoptimization of the limiter, after which the pressure bound and all claims survive, so the loss is limited but not routine.

temporal accuracy

While formally restricted to second-order temporal accuracy

Although this conventional scaling restricts the temporal accuracy to second order at the two-phase interface due to the operator splitting

issues.failure_explanation: The paper states that Strang splitting plus the implicit solver give only second-order temporal accuracy, and that the tests use dt proportional to dx. The temporal error is then O(dt^2)=O(dx^2), which dominates the third-order spatial error O(dx^3) of DG(P^2) asymptotically, so the temporal error cannot remain subdominant and third-order convergence is not the expected asymptotic rate. The stated justification and the resulting accuracy promise are mathematically inconsistent with the paper's own order statement (the test case is two-phase throughout, z1=0.5+0.4 sin(pi x), so the O(dt^2) splitting error is active everywhere).

failure_location.quote:

As a result, the  DG($P^2$) with $\Delta t \propto \Delta x$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either rerun the convergence study with dt = O(dx^(3/2)) (so that O(dt^2)=O(dx^3)) and state the rate accordingly, or weaken the claim to second-order asymptotic accuracy with observed orders near three on the tested grids.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised third-order convergence of DG(P^2) with dt proportional to dx and the interpretation of the reported convergence table are unsupported; only second-order asymptotic accuracy is implied by the stated temporal order.
issues.title: Third-order convergence with dt proportional to dx conflicts with second-order time accuracy
issues.why_classification: Adjusting the time-step scaling (or the accompanying rate statement) is a short local repair that preserves the method, its rates and its advertised scope, with no new lemma, construction or replacement argument.
